bog-of-allen-nature-centre: The Irish Peatland Conservation Council's centre, with a frog garden, a walkable bog and exhibitions about peatlands.
castletown-house: A Palladian mansion of 1722, the largest in Ireland, with restored halls and parkland open to the public.
irish-national-stud-japanese-gardens: The national stud farm with champion stallions, a horse museum and the famous Japanese Gardens of 1906.
curraghchase-forest-park: A forest park with the ruins of the De Vere mansion, trails, a lake and a protected bat colony.
lough-gur: A kidney-shaped lake surrounded by megaliths, stone circles and the Grange Stone Circle, the largest in Ireland.
foynes-flying-boat-museum: A museum on the former Pan Am base, with a full-size replica Boeing 314 and the origins of Irish Coffee.
adare-village: A village considered Ireland's prettiest, with thatched cottages, monasteries and the Desmond castle.
st-marys-cathedral-limerick: A cathedral of 1168, Limerick's oldest building still in use, with rare medieval misericords.
hunt-museum: The Hunts' collection of art and antiquities, with Picasso, Renoir, Leonardo da Vinci and Celtic artefacts.
king-johns-castle-limerick: A Norman castle of 1210 on the banks of the Shannon, with interactive exhibitions on sieges and medieval history.
holy-cross-abbey: A restored 12th-century Cistercian abbey, famous for the relic of the True Cross and still a place of worship.
mitchelstown-cave: One of Europe's largest caves, with giant stalactites, vast chambers and concert-hall acoustics.
ormond-castle: Ireland's only Elizabethan manor house, built by Thomas Butler, 10th Earl of Ormond, alongside medieval towers.
the-vee-bay-lough: A V-shaped mountain pass with a viewpoint over the Suir valley and the glacial lake Bay Lough.
glen-of-aherlow: A scenic valley between the Galtee Mountains, with trails, the Christ the King viewpoint and charming villages.
swiss-cottage: An ornamental cottage of 1810, a perfect example of the "picturesque" style, with a restored interior and woodland.
cahir-castle: One of Ireland's best-preserved castles, from the 13th century, on an island in the River Suir.
rock-of-cashel: A spectacular medieval complex on a limestone outcrop: Gothic cathedral, Romanesque chapel and round tower.
tintern-abbey-wexford: A Cistercian abbey founded in 1200 by William Marshal, with a Victorian colonnade and a wooded valley.
ferns-castle: A 13th-century Norman castle with a cruciform chapel and modern stained glass, in the former capital of the kings of Leinster.
wexford-wildfowl-reserve: A nature reserve on the North Slob, winter home to one third of the world's Greenland white-fronted geese.
curracloe-beach: An 11 km stretch of fine sandy beach, location of the opening of "Saving Private Ryan", with dunes and trails.
saltee-islands: A seabird sanctuary with one of Ireland's largest gannet colonies, reachable by boat from Kilmore Quay.
dunbrody-famine-ship: A faithful replica of a Great Famine emigrant ship, with an immersive tour of the Atlantic crossing.
hook-lighthouse: A medieval lighthouse in operation since the 13th century — one of the oldest in the world — with tours and a café.
